findings:
🟡 [wdog-bare-pid-fallback] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_watchdog_signal_worker` falls back to `kill -$sig "$target"` (bare pid) when the pgid kill fails; on every path WORKER_SID is constructed as a pgid (setsid leader, `set -m` pgid, or the `setsid --wait` child leader), so the group kill failing means the tree is already dead and the fallback can only hit a recycled pid inside the microsecond window between the sleeper's token check and `rm -f "$tok"` in `_wait_worker_with_watchdog`. Also, if `_setsid_wait_worker_sid` ever falls back to `$rp` (supervisor pid, not a pgid), the bare-pid fallback TERMs only the supervisor and orphans the worker while still reporting `timed_out=true`. Smallest remediation: delete the `|| kill "-$sig" "$target"` fallback. Excluded from this version: the recycle window is not reachable in practice and the poll (20×50ms plus /proc children) makes the supervisor fallback effectively unreachable; the guards against `$$` and the dispatcher pgid are present and correct.
🟡 [wdog-deadline-coincidence] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If the worker exits 0 in the same instant the sleeper wakes, the watchdog sees the token still present, writes `.fired`, and the run is classified `failure`/`timed_out=true` despite a clean exit. Sub-millisecond window; commit/diff fields still reflect the real branch. Not blocking.
🟡 [no-setsid-set-m-side-effects] CUT/FOLLOW-UP On hosts without `setsid` the plain/detached fallback runs `set -m` permanently for the rest of the script (job-control `[1] pid`/`Done` notices on stderr, background jobs in new pgids); if `set -m` fails (no tty, `|| true`) WORKER_SID becomes the dispatcher's own pgid and `_watchdog_signal_worker` silently no-ops, so the bound is unenforced on that host rather than unsafe. The unnamed `sleep "$secs" &` branch also isn't covered by the `pkill -f` sweep if TERM lands before `sp=$!`. Linux hosts always have util-linux setsid, so this is out of the practical envelope.
🔵 [output-comment-default-never-emitted] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The OUTPUT contract comment lists `"timeout_source": "default"` for the result JSON, but `emit()` only writes `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_source` when TIMEOUT_SOURCE is non-empty, so the result never carries `default` (only the manifest does). Doc-only inaccuracy; tests assert `default` on the manifest, which is correct.
🔵 [detached-stop-reach] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The detached-child path now runs the worker in its own setsid session instead of in-session; any external stop/reaper that kills the detached dispatcher's session/pgid via the manifest `pid` will no longer reach the worker tree on that path (the `return 0` before `reap_container` is unchanged). Spec-mandated isolation; not provable from this diff whether a stop path relies on session co-membership — verify separately.
